claim: A published platform used inducible CRISPR interference and activation in human iPSC-derived microglia, including pooled screens and a single-cell transcriptomic readout, establishing an external technical precedent for bidirectional perturbation in a human microglial model.
future_grounding_route: Treat this only as platform-feasibility context. A project-relevant route would require an independently designed human donor screen with predeclared perturbations, CRISPRi and CRISPRa directions, controls, held-out perturbations, and orthogonal functional readouts.
project_use: External method context for a future direction-resolving human microglia experiment; not evidence for any MS target or progression mechanism.
relationship_note: The method could address the project's missing intervention-direction evidence, but the source does not test the project's candidates or establish MS therapeutic relevance.

source.citation: Dräger et al. A CRISPRi/a platform in human iPSC-derived microglia uncovers regulators of disease states. Nature Neuroscience. 2022.
source.label: Human iPSC-derived microglia CRISPRi/a platform

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Publisher page metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute article text.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the external platform or run its own human microglia perturbation screen.
